subject: Retention window and deterministic scrub strategy for audit request
messages:

Date: 2027-01-10T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention requirements for EU clinical pilot

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this — Medicorp is preparing for a regional audit and we need a clear position from Redwood on two things for the EU pilot: (1) retention limits we can guarantee per data category (PII vs PHI) and (2) a deterministic redaction strategy we can show auditors that ensures erased records cannot be reconstructed.

The pilot will ingest EHR snippets and patient identifiers; regulators will expect: a documented retention window, a scrub procedure (field-level and record-level), and proof-of-erasure artifacts.

Can you outline the recommended retention ceilings and the scrub approaches you support (masking, irreversible hashing, field removal, tokenization, etc.)? Also, what evidence can Redwood provide (logs, erasure reports, hashes) and how long you retain those evidence artifacts?

We are hoping to share a concise one-page summary with our compliance team by Monday.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Huang
Compliance Manager, Medicorp Health
+44 20 7946 0123
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medicorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-10T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention requirements for EU clinical pilot

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Quick notes up front, and I'll loop in Karthik for the technical/implementation details.

- Retention ceilings: hosted API defaults are 30 days for request/response content; for Private deployments we can support customer-defined windows down to a 0-day (no retention) policy. For regulated PHI we recommend an explicit contracted minimum (e.g., 90 days) if you need short-term replay/QA, otherwise 0–30 days is typical.
- Scrub strategies we support: field-level redaction (configurable), irreversible hashing with salt (deterministic for matching), and complete record purging. We also support a selective retention policy per field type via routing tags.
- Evidence: erasure run logs, per-record deletion hashes, and archival audit reports. Retention of evidence artifacts is typically 1 year by default but can be shortened or extended contractually.

Karthik — can you confirm the scrub rule capabilities we can deliver in the EU Private deployment and attach the matrix we use for recommended windows? Also, Laura — could you provide the one-page compliance summary (legal language) we can share with Medicorp?

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks

Hi all — technical detail below, keeping it practical for the auditor checklist. Attaching our retention matrix and an example scrub rule (CSV/YAML).

1) Retention ceilings (recommendation):
   - Identifier fields (name, national id): 0–30 days (default 0 for highest assurance, 30 if short-term QA needed).
   - Clinical notes (de-identified): 90 days if linked workspace requires model tuning; otherwise 30 days.
   - PHI (diagnoses, meds) embedded in free text: treated as PHI; recommend 30–90 days depending on business need.

2) Scrub options we offer (supported in Private and Dedicated deployments):
   - Field-level redact: configurable rules remove/replace values before persistence.
   - Deterministic irreversible hashing: HMAC-SHA256 with customer-provided salt; stored hashes allow match-on-write but not reconstruction.
   - Cryptographic tokenization: reversible via KMS if customer opts to retain re-identification keys (recommended for research workflows only).
   - Aggregation/minimization: redact or truncate sensitive spans + explicit retention tags.

3) Erasure evidence and integrity:
   - Per-tenant deletion records (deletion job id, timestamp, filter criteria) retained as audit log.
   - Deletion-proof artifacts: salted hashes of deleted record ids with signed timestamps (log entry).
   - Optional snapshot of pre-erase index (hashed) to demonstrate scope.

4) Completeness SLOs and guarantees:
   - Logical deletion: immediate (SLA: within minutes); physical data purge from storage: within contracted window (typical: 7–30 days) depending on backup/replica retention policies.
   - For high-assurance erasure (no backup retention), we can propose a 30-day backup window and a contractual commitment to purge backups within 30 days after deletion request.

Attachments referenced: redwood-eu-retention-matrix.csv, example-scrub-rule.yaml

Open questions for Medicorp:
 - Do you require reversible tokenization for any research use cases?
 - Do you want evidence artifacts retained longer than 1 year?

Dylan/Karthik — helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Medicorp does not want reversible tokenization for the pilot (so reversible KMS-backed tokens are out). Deterministic hashing + salt is acceptable if we can control the salt (customer-managed).
- We need a contractual commitment on backup purge timing. Can Redwood commit to physical purge of backups within 30 days of a certified deletion request? If not, we need explicit language on backup retention windows.
- For audit evidence, our legal team will want signed timestamps and a digest proof. I'm adding Timothy from Legal to the thread.

Could you draft the one-page summary we can hand to our compliance team by end of day Monday?

Thanks — Claire
